verdicts.reason: Quote states hosts are not required to drive valid low; MAY/scenario fine.
Quote says devices can tolerate shorter reset windows.
Routing function of address only is a 'must'; but checking requires scenario (routing is not checkable from interface signals per cycle by assertion alone). Keep MUST, check scenario.
Optional use of source IDs for reordering; stated.
Design-time guidance for fabric architect; nothing to verify at runtime.
Design-time guidance for fabric architect; nothing to verify or exercise.
Recommendation to add assertions in the design; not a testable behaviour of the interface, and a_source loss is not observable from interface alone.
Hosts must not assume all AIW bits returned; it is a restriction (use only low bits). Not checkable by assertion; scenario is appropriate.
Devices must return a_source on d_source; checkable.
Fabric should pass user bits blindly (quote says 'should'); not relying on them is a statement of fact. Strength SHOULD.

Timing relationship between user and source bits is checkable only for the transport through the fabric, not as an interface assertion by any actor; it describes the channel alignment. Better as scenario.
Project-level assignment policy; nothing to verify at this interface.
Vague, project-specific; no concrete verifiable behaviour.
Descriptive of opcode encoding; permissive and nothing specific to verify.
Hosts do not use non-contiguous masks; restriction checkable from a_mask.
Devices have the right to assert d_error for unsupported masks.
Quote says a_size should be 'h2.
Quote describes the encoding 2^a_size; it is a definition, hard to assert on a_size alone, but the encoding relation is stated. Strength is not explicit; treat as scenario.
Quote says a_mask should indicate valid byte lanes.
Quote: devices should return an error for undefined opcodes.
Undefined d_opcode is a device response; the actor that sends it is the slave, and the rule is that it is undefined. Actor corrected to slave and treated as a restriction on responses.
Devices check wrong opcode and raise d_error.
Two requirements: host must not issue a_size>2; device raises d_error. Actor of the d_error behaviour is the slave.
The d_error behaviour is the device's; actor slave.
The d_error behaviour is the device's; actor slave.
Devices raise d_error for non-existent addresses.
Quote says may lead to error depending on support.
Register files assume aligned 32-bit accesses; this is a constraint on requests (host must issue aligned 32-bit accesses).
Host discards orphaned/wrong-opcode responses; quote says 'will be discarded'.
Planned, unimplemented feature; nothing to verify.
Optional, unspecified additional checks; nothing to verify.

questions.question: Hosts never use non-contiguous masks, yet devices may or may not error on them. Should the testbench ever drive non-contiguous masks, and what response is expected?
Are the illegal-request cases host obligations or device-checked errors? Is d_error mandatory for every violation or only for the listed checks?
a_size should be 2 for PutFullData but must not exceed 2 in general. Is a smaller size for PutFullData allowed?
